newsitem.title: UK: UK budget makes rate rise less likely - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: UK budget makes rate rise less likely - Treasury.

text.p: Britain's annual budget, delivered by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Tuesday, makes it less likely interest rate rises will be needed in the near future, Treasury minister Phillip Oppenheim said.
Asked if the budget tax cuts increased the chances of interest rate rises, Oppenheim told Reuters Financial Television: "I think it makes it less likely."
"The Chancellor steered a very good course. This is a reasonably tight budget," he added.

Clarke unveiled a modest one percentage point cut in the basic rate of income tax but offset about two billion pounds of tax cuts in all with about the same amount of planned spending cuts and tax increases elsewhere.

"If you look at the way the markets reacted, I think that confirms it," Oppenheim said. "If this had been a loose budget you would have seen real problems with the long (bond) rates zooming up. That has not happened."
A Reuter poll of 35 London-based economists conducted after the budget produced a consensus expecting base rates, now at six percent, to end next year at seven percent.
At least a quarter-point of that increase is likely to come before elections that are due within six months.
Oppenheim said Clarke would take no risks with inflation. "He will do what's necessary if he thinks there is any danger of inflation taking off."

"We're all politicians, we all have to have an eye on the election, it would be silly to deny that, but the Chancellor's priority is that the strong growth...continues and is sustainable," Oppenheim said.
